internal.title: Incident Report: Checkout Service Error Rate Spike Due to Payment Service Flag
internal.body:
At 12:24 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Investigation identified the root cause as an error injection in the payment service caused by the paymentFailure flag being set to 100%, resulting in all payment requests failing with 'Invalid token' errors. This caused a knock-on effect leading to elevated errors in the checkout service.

The flag was disabled at 12:44 UTC after approval, leading to immediate recovery and normalization of error rates. The incident was resolved promptly with no lasting impact on customer transactions.

Key timeline:
- 12:24:52: Alert received for high error rate in checkout
- 12:44:38: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection
- 12:44:48: Flag paymentFailure disabled after approval
- 12:44:48: Verified recovery with error rates returning to normal

Actions taken:
- Disabled the paymentFailure flag
- Monitored service metrics to confirm recovery

This incident highlights the importance of flag management and rapid diagnosis in preventing cascading failures across dependent services.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing issue
external.body: Between 12:24 and 12:44 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to a problem in the payment processing system. Our team identified and resolved the issue promptly by disabling a configuration that was causing payment requests to fail. The checkout service error rates returned to normal shortly after, and the issue is now resolved. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.
